record.paper_title: Jaynes–Cummings Model and a Non–Commutative “Geometry” : A Few Problems Noted
record.context_brief: General theory of singularity removal under non-commutativization
record.original_question: For classical models with singular objects such as singular points or singular lines, can one find many examples in which passing to a non-commutative model makes those singularities milder or removes them partly, and can one construct a general theory explaining when this removal or mitigation occurs?

evidence.quote: It is probable that a non–commutative model makes singular objects (singular points or singular lines or etc) in the corresponding classical model mild or removes them partly.

More generally, it is probable that a singularity (singularities) in some classical model is (are) removed in the process of non–commutativization. Further study on both finding many examples and constructing a general theory will be required.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider classical mathematical or physical models whose underlying spaces (or solution sets) contain singular objects such as singular points, singular lines, or other lower-dimensional singular loci. A "non-commutative deformation" of such a model is a replacement of its commutative algebra of functions (or of its phase space, configuration space, or coordinate ring) by a non-commutative algebra depending on one or more deformation parameters, in such a way that the original commutative model is recovered in an appropriate classical limit.

(a) Exhibit a large family of explicit examples of classical models possessing singularities (e.g. singular algebraic varieties, singular symplectic spaces, classical field configurations with point or line singularities) together with non-commutative deformations of those models in which the singularities are either entirely removed or rendered milder (e.g. by becoming smooth in the non-commutative sense, by acquiring finite-dimensional local algebras of regular functions, or by having well-defined non-commutative resolutions).

(b) Formulate and prove a general theory predicting, intrinsically from the classical data (such as the type of singularity, the Poisson structure underlying the deformation, or cohomological invariants), precisely when a non-commutative deformation removes or mitigates a given classical singularity, and characterize the residual singular structure when complete removal is impossible.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a broad research program rather than a precise conjecture. While various specific instances of singularity resolution via non-commutative deformation are known (e.g. non-commutative crepant resolutions in algebraic geometry, fuzzy spheres replacing singular orbifolds, and smoothing of cone singularities in non-commutative field theory), no comprehensive general theory characterizing exactly when non-commutativization removes classical singularities has been established. The problem therefore remains open in its general form.

status_evidence.title: Non-commutative crepant resolutions
status_evidence.snippet: Van den Bergh's non-commutative crepant resolutions provide non-commutative algebras resolving certain singular varieties, an instance of the phenomenon.
status_evidence.claim: Specific examples of non-commutative resolutions of singularities exist, but a fully general theory remains absent.
